episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — August 11, 2026
episodes.summary: The tape looks quiet this week. Bitcoin is pinned near $64,000. But underneath that calm is a structural stress story, not a calm one, and it starts with the largest corporate bitcoin holder on earth turning into a seller.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: The model race is still stalled near the top of the leaderboards. So this week the competition moved down a layer, to who can finance the compute those models run on — and Nvidia just moved to own that layer directly.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: We left the Fed's three-way fork unresolved on Tuesday, and this morning's July CPI print was supposed to be the tiebreaker. It wasn't clean. Headline CPI rose 0.20% month over month, holding the annual rate steady at 2.7%, which reads as roughly in line. Core CPI did not cooperate.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: The institutionalization trade has a new problem this week, and it isn't price. It's economics. Two of the cleanest public proxies for the digital-dollar stack, Circle and Coinbase, both reported earnings that show the machinery underneath slowing down, just as the regulatory tailwinds were supposed to speed it up.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: The Federal Reserve's independence is under direct political attack again, and this time the target is the Board itself, not just the reaction function.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has described SK hynix as memory's scarcity king, the company writing full-passthrough pricing into its contracts on the strength of a sold-out HBM roadmap. Today that lead gets its first real challenge, and it comes from two directions at once: a rival's yield curve, and SK hynix's own labor floor.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: The last several days on this show ran on a single idea: agent unit cost is racing toward zero, and value is migrating below the model. Today the marginal news moves up the stack. It's not about cheaper agents.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the binding constraint on enterprise AI keeps climbing the stack. First it was whether demand was real. Then whether capacity could serve it. Then whether usage converts to revenue. This week's evidence says the frontier has moved one level further: can enterprises even measure the return.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: We spent Monday on Tempus selling its models and data as a standalone product. Today the buyer side of that same trade showed up: a top-five pharma company just committed its infrastructure to agentic AI at scale.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: This beat spent the last week watching capital and regulators move faster than proven economics. Zoox got the first-ever federal exemption for a steering-wheel-free robotaxi and started charging fares in Las Vegas.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — August 12, 2026
episodes.summary: SpaceX reported its first quarterly results as a public company this week, and the numbers rewrite how you should think about the company. Total revenue hit $7.8 billion in the second quarter, up 92% from $4 billion a year earlier. That is the headline. The twist is where the growth came from.
